title: Type That Reads
intro: 45 to 90 characters a line, 120 to 145% line spacing, and one emphasis at a time.

learn.title: Body text first
learn.text:
Readers spend their time in body text.

On screen: **15–25 px** size, **120–145%** line spacing, **45–90 characters** a line, spaces included.

learn.title: A small scale
learn.text:
Pick from a scale such as 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 30, 36, 48 px.

Use **two or three sizes per component**. Weights with a job: regular body, medium labels, semibold buttons, bold headings.

try.q: How many type sizes should one component use?
try.explain: Enough for hierarchy, few enough to stay calm.

learn.title: Emphasis
learn.text:
**Bold or italic, sparingly and not together.**
Underline only links.
All caps for less than a line, with 5–12% extra letter spacing.

learn.title: UI text is scanned
learn.text:
Reading rules come from long text. Interface text is scanned: **front-load** the words that matter and keep labels short.

Help pages and empty states still follow the reading rules.

try.q: Where do long-text reading rules still apply in a product?
try.explain: Anything more than a couple of lines is read.

test.q: What line spacing suits body text?
test.explain: Tighter for headings, roomier for body.

test.q: What body size range works on screen?
test.explain: Product UI body rarely goes below 16 px.

test.q: Bold and italic together on one phrase:
How should all-caps text be set?
options: Short, with a little extra letter spacing
Only in the body font’s light weight
test.explain: Less than a line, 5–12% extra spacing.

test.q: Which is a typographic detail readers notice?
options: Straight quotes instead of curly ones
The colour of the scroll bar
Whether the CSS uses rem units
test.explain: Use curly quotes and real apostrophes.

test.q: Wide screens most often break which rule?
test.explain: Long lines make the eye lose its place.
